resources.string: Starts a local VPN tap that sees only WhatsApp\'s own traffic, forwards it unchanged, and lists the IP addresses, ports and protocols it uses. No root needed.
1) Tap Start and approve the VPN request. 2) Place or receive a WhatsApp call for a few seconds. 3) Open the results.
Now use WhatsApp: start a voice or video call.

Android will ask you to allow a VPN connection. This VPN is local: only WhatsApp\'s traffic is routed through the app, it is forwarded to the normal network unchanged, and nothing is uploaded.\n\nThe app reads packet headers (addresses, ports, sizes) to build the report. Message and call contents are end-to-end encrypted and cannot be read. Use it only on your own device and calls.
Open a .pcap or .pcapng file recorded elsewhere (for example with Wireshark or tcpdump). It is analysed on this device only.
No results yet. Run a live analysis or import a capture file.
Look-ups are optional and sent to the public RDAP registry service (rdap.org); only public IP addresses are sent.

Important: addresses marked "peer candidate" are only candidates. WhatsApp calls are often relayed through Meta servers, and a candidate can be a VPN, carrier gateway or relay rather than the other person.
Registry data: shows where the address block is registered, not a person\'s location.
Your own public address(es) seen in STUN: %1$s
Address belongs to a known Meta (Facebook/WhatsApp) range
Resolved from a WhatsApp/Meta host name
Registry lists Meta/Facebook as the owner
UDP traffic flows in both directions
Public address outside known Meta ranges

The app reports evidence, not certainty. It does not reveal or prove the other person\'s IP address. WhatsApp usually relays calls through Meta servers; a direct peer-to-peer path is used only sometimes, and even then the address may belong to a VPN, a mobile carrier gateway (CGNAT) or a relay. Country and ISP come from registry records and do not show a physical location.

All processing happens on your device. No account, no analytics, no uploads. Only WhatsApp\'s traffic is routed through the local VPN. The optional live PCAP keeps just the first 96 bytes of each packet in the app\'s private cache and is removed when the app\'s data is cleared. The only network request the app makes itself is the optional registry look-up you start.

• IPv4 traffic is analysed live; IPv6 traffic bypasses the VPN tap (use a PCAP for IPv6).\n• Meta address ranges are a built-in snapshot and may become outdated.\n• Calls made over a different VPN or when another VPN is active cannot be captured.
WhatsApp is not installed on this device
Local VPN tap is active. Tap to open.
